purpose: Generated board-ready index for file-based asks/offers templates.

publication.relay: static host, repository discussion, or other dumb relay
publication.privacy: Do not publish private contact details, exact addresses, beneficiary identities, or sensitive threat models in this file.

principles: templates are not live help claims
no private contact details in public files
asks and offers point back to sourced guides, categories, or initiatives
a relay may move the file but must not become the authority

items.title: We need help running a digital-safety clinic
items.summary: A library, community group, or mutual-aid group needs help with safer messaging, passwords, 2FA, VPN basics, and a handout people can actually use.
items.prompt: Can you help run a calm digital-safety session for people who do not want jargon?

guides.title: Digital literacy: attention, data, and control
Private messaging: encryption, metadata, and reach
Password managers: security, recovery, and trust
VPNs: threat models, trust, and jurisdiction

initiatives.name: Electronic Frontier Foundation
initiatives.description: Defends digital privacy, free expression, and innovation through litigation, advocacy, and open-source tools.

legitimacy.line: Electronic Frontier Foundation: Defends digital privacy, free expression, and innovation through litigation, advocacy, and open-source tools.

source.note: EFF describes itself as a leading nonprofit defending digital privacy, free speech and innovation.

initiatives.name: Library Freedom Project
initiatives.description: A library-worker network turning privacy, intellectual freedom and information democracy into trainings, resources and local advocacy inside public institutions.

legitimacy.line: Library Freedom Project: A library-worker network turning privacy, intellectual freedom and information democracy into trainings, resources and local advocacy inside public institutions.

source.note: LFP trains library workers and communities on privacy, intellectual freedom and information democracy.

initiatives.name: Signal Foundation
initiatives.description: Maintains nonprofit privacy infrastructure for encrypted messaging, with strong open-source signals and a narrower donation path.

legitimacy.line: Signal Foundation: Maintains nonprofit privacy infrastructure for encrypted messaging, with strong open-source signals and a narrower donation path.

source.note: Signal Foundation says it makes private communication accessible, secure, and ubiquitous through nonprofit privacy technology.

receipts.note: EFF publishes Surveillance Self-Defense as public digital-security guidance for people and groups.
Library Freedom Project publishes resources for privacy and intellectual freedom work in libraries.

limits: Do not publish a group's threat model or participant names.
Do not imply the facilitator can provide legal or emergency safety advice.

items.title: We need help checking a fundraiser before we share it
items.summary: A local group wants a quick accountability check before amplifying a fundraiser or emergency giving appeal.
items.prompt: Can you help us check the organizer identity, payment route, recipient clarity, fees, and update pattern before we share this?

initiatives.name: BBB Wise Giving Alliance / Give.org
initiatives.description: A standards-based charity accountability resource for checking governance, finances, transparency, appeals and results reporting.

legitimacy.line: BBB Wise Giving Alliance / Give.org: A standards-based charity accountability resource for checking governance, finances, transparency, appeals and results reporting.

source.note: Give.org is most valuable as a standards-based trust screen, not as a direct ranking of which charities do the most good.

initiatives.name: GiveDirectly
initiatives.description: Delivers donations as direct, unconditional cash transfers to people in poverty, backed by randomized trials.

legitimacy.line: GiveDirectly: Delivers donations as direct, unconditional cash transfers to people in poverty, backed by randomized trials.

source.note: GiveWell's review describes unconditional cash transfers as evidence-backed and supported by randomized controlled trials.

initiatives.name: TechSoup
initiatives.description: A nonprofit technology-access network helping civil society organizations get software, training and digital capacity support.

legitimacy.line: TechSoup: A nonprofit technology-access network helping civil society organizations get software, training and digital capacity support.

source.note: TechSoup provides nonprofit technology access, validation, training and donated/discounted software through a global network.

receipts.note: The FTC's charity guidance tells donors to check charity names, payment methods, and fundraiser claims before giving.
BBB Wise Giving Alliance publishes charity accountability standards that can inform lightweight due-diligence checks.

limits: Do not publish recipient medical, immigration, housing, or safety details.
Do not present a quick check as a formal audit.

items.title: I can share a one-page giving research brief
items.summary: I can make a short source list for people comparing evidence-backed giving, climate giving, or local commitments before a fundraising season.
items.prompt: I can turn public giving research into a one-page brief that keeps impact, transparency, and local commitments separate.

initiatives.name: GiveWell
initiatives.description: A research nonprofit that rigorously finds the highest-impact giving opportunities and routes donations to them.

legitimacy.line: GiveWell: A research nonprofit that rigorously finds the highest-impact giving opportunities and routes donations to them.

source.note: GiveWell's mission is to find giving opportunities that save or improve lives the most per dollar.

initiatives.name: Giving What We Can
initiatives.description: A public effective-giving community that helps donors choose researched charities, pledge recurring giving, and compare high-impact cause areas.

legitimacy.line: Giving What We Can: A public effective-giving community that helps donors choose researched charities, pledge recurring giving, and compare high-impact cause areas.

source.note: Giving What We Can helps donors find effective charities backed by research and routes attention toward high-impact giving opportunities.

initiatives.name: Giving Green
initiatives.description: A climate-donation evaluator focused on high-impact nonprofits, policy change, and public research for donors.

legitimacy.line: Giving Green: A climate-donation evaluator focused on high-impact nonprofits, policy change, and public research for donors.

source.note: Giving Green evaluates climate nonprofits against scale, feasibility and funding need to guide high-impact climate donations.

initiatives.name: Against Malaria Foundation
initiatives.description: A GiveWell top charity that funds and tracks insecticide-treated bed nets to prevent malaria, publishing every distribution.

legitimacy.line: Against Malaria Foundation: A GiveWell top charity that funds and tracks insecticide-treated bed nets to prevent malaria, publishing every distribution.

source.note: GiveWell describes AMF as funding insecticide-treated nets for malaria prevention in low- and middle-income countries.

initiatives.name: GiveDirectly
initiatives.description: Delivers donations as direct, unconditional cash transfers to people in poverty, backed by randomized trials.

legitimacy.line: GiveDirectly: Delivers donations as direct, unconditional cash transfers to people in poverty, backed by randomized trials.

source.note: GiveWell's review describes unconditional cash transfers as evidence-backed and supported by randomized controlled trials.

receipts.note: GiveWell publishes a top-charities list and research pages for highly cost-effective giving opportunities.
Giving What We Can publishes cause-area guidance for donors comparing global health, animal welfare, climate, and other areas.

limits: Do not imply the brief is personal financial, tax, or legal advice.
Do not collapse local relationship-based giving into cost-effectiveness scoring.

items.title: We need help choosing a repair-first phone or laptop
items.summary: A household, school, or small organization wants to compare repair, reuse, refurbished options, software support, and total cost before buying.
items.prompt: Can you help us compare repairability, software support, used or refurbished options, and total cost before we replace devices?

guides.title: Phones: support life, repairability, and privacy
Laptops: repairability, upgrades, and support life
Right to repair: keeping devices in use

initiatives.name: Software Freedom Conservancy
initiatives.description: A nonprofit home and legal/policy advocate for free and open-source software projects, copyleft compliance and software right-to-repair.

legitimacy.line: Software Freedom Conservancy: A nonprofit home and legal/policy advocate for free and open-source software projects, copyleft compliance and software right-to-repair.

source.note: Software Freedom Conservancy provides nonprofit homes and services for free and open-source software projects and advocates for software freedom.

initiatives.name: Open Source Initiative
initiatives.description: A standards-and-governance nonprofit for the open-source ecosystem, especially useful when you want to support the shared definition and licensing norms behind reusable software.

legitimacy.line: Open Source Initiative: A standards-and-governance nonprofit for the open-source ecosystem, especially useful when you want to support the shared definition and licensing norms behind reusable software.

source.note: OSI describes itself as a global nonprofit educating, advocating and building bridges across the open-source community.

initiatives.name: Consumer Federation of America
initiatives.description: A U.S. consumer-advocacy federation working through research, policy, education and coalition action, including privacy, AI and marketplace fairness.

legitimacy.line: Consumer Federation of America: A U.S. consumer-advocacy federation working through research, policy, education and coalition action, including privacy, AI and marketplace fairness.

source.note: CFA advances consumer interests across policy areas including AI, data privacy, financial services, food, insurance and product safety.

receipts.note: iFixit publishes repairability material for electronics, including phones and laptops.
The FTC's Nixing the Fix report describes repair restrictions as a consumer and competition issue.

limits: Do not ask volunteers to handle devices containing private data without a wipe plan.
Do not present repairability as a substitute for safety recalls or warranty rights.
